text:
John von Neumann was a child prodigy born in Budapest, Kingdom of Hungary, in 1903, whose early mathematical talent was recognized by tutors. He advanced rapidly, publishing significant mathematical papers by age 19, including work that provided the modern definition of ordinal numbers. He received advanced education at the University of Budapest and later studied mathematics under David Hilbert at the University of Göttingen.
Von Neumann made foundational contributions across multiple fields, including founding game theory with his 1928 minimax theorem, and revolutionizing mathematics through his work on set theory, where he developed the axiom of foundation and the notion of class. In physics, he established the rigorous mathematical framework for quantum mechanics with his 1932 work, and his contributions to fluid dynamics included the Taylor–von Neumann–Sedov blast wave solution. His work in computer science led to the conception of the single-memory, stored-program architecture, known as the von Neumann architecture.
